title: Sharp-Crested Weir Discharge (Rectangular)

L.description: Effective crest length (subtract end contractions if present)

H.description: Head on weir (water surface above crest)

applicability: Standard weir equation. For suppressed weir (L = channel width), Cd ≈ 0.611. With end contractions, effective L = L - 0.1nH where n = number of contractions. Must have free-fall (aeration) downstream of nappe.

title: Broad-Crested Weir Discharge
equation: Q = Cd × L × H^1.5  where Cd ≈ 1.6 (SI)
applicability: Crest length in flow direction ≥ 2–3 × H for broad-crested behavior. Cd varies with H/crest-length ratio. Used for check structures, division weirs.

title: Parshall Flume Discharge (Free Flow)

Ha.description: Upstream head (gauge reading at 2/3 A from throat)

applicability: Free-flow condition: submergence ratio Hb/Ha < transition submergence (60–80% depending on size). For submerged flow, correction factor applied. Standard sizes from 1 inch to 50 feet throat width.

title: Constant-Head Orifice (CHO) Discharge
applicability: USBR CHO turnout maintains constant Δh by adjusting upstream check. Measurement accuracy ±5% with proper maintenance. Δh typically 0.06–0.15 m (0.2–0.5 ft).
source: USBR Design of Small Canal Structures

title: Vertical Drop — Pool Depth (Momentum Balance)
applicability: Belanger equation for sequent depth. Stilling pool must be deep enough to contain the jump. Pool length ≈ 4–6 × d₂. USBR provides standard designs for small drops.
source: Belanger (1828), USBR Design of Small Canal Structures

title: Baffled Drop — USBR Design Criteria

q_max.description: Maximum unit discharge for baffle design

applicability: USBR baffled apron drop. Baffle height typically 0.8 × critical depth. Baffle rows spaced at 2× baffle height, staggered. Chute slope 2H:1V. Upstream sill, end sill at toe.
source: USBR Design of Small Canal Structures, Peterka (1984)

title: Inverted Siphon — Head Loss

hf.description: Friction loss = f × L/D × V²/(2g) or Manning/Hazen-Williams

applicability: Available head = difference in canal water surface elevation upstream and downstream. Head loss must not exceed available head. Minimum velocity 1.0 m/s to prevent sedimentation. Maximum velocity 3.0 m/s.
source: USBR Design of Small Canal Structures

title: Pipe Drop — Inlet Control Head

c, n.description: Coefficients depending on inlet type (from FHWA HDS-5)

applicability: FHWA inlet control nomographs also used for pipe drops and culvert crossings. Check both inlet and outlet control — governing condition produces higher headwater.
source: FHWA HDS-5 (Hydraulic Design of Highway Culverts)

title: Side Wasteway — Lateral Spillway Discharge

dQ/dx.description: Discharge per unit length of side weir

Cd.description: Side weir discharge coefficient (0.33–0.40, lower than frontal weir)

y.description: Water depth in canal at the weir location

P.description: Side weir crest height above canal invert

applicability: Side weir discharge coefficient is lower than for frontal (normal) weirs because of oblique approach flow. Total wasteway discharge obtained by integrating over the weir length. For design, often simplified with average head.

title: Siphon Spillway — Priming Head and Discharge

H_net.description: Net head (difference between upstream and downstream levels minus losses)

applicability: Siphon spillways activate automatically when water rises above the priming level. Discharge jumps from zero to full capacity over a small head range (~0.1–0.3 m). Air vent at crown controls priming elevation. Used for canal wasteways and reservoir emergency spillways.
